exposure: percutaneous image-guided single-probe cryoablation using liquid nitrogen
outcome: lesion resolution/ablation zone coverage (measured by MRI and clinical follow-up)
cohort: The study included 14 patients (mean age: 39.6 years) with symptomatic abdominal wall endometriosis who underwent percutaneous cryoablation.
finding: Percutaneous cryoablation using a single probe with liquid nitrogen was found to be a safe and effective treatment for abdominal wall endometriosis, leading to significant pain relief and minimal complications.
